page.layout: One column of text, full width. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Signature "L 2" and catchword "ris," at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Et si nondum Ira tua auferatur, sed manus tua adhuc extenditur, vertatur (oro) contra Me, & contra domum Patris mei, oves autem istæ quid fecerunt?
Satient mcæ[?] perpessiones eorum Malitiam qui sunt mihi pariter & Ecclesiæ infensi; Sed nec ultima eorum sævitia Charitatem meam unquam exuperet.
Procul à Me facessat omnis vindictæ cogitatio, nec mihi percat patientiæ merces, tibi Gloria.
Quemadmodum mihi cor dedisti ad condonandum facile, ita & Tu (precor) condones, quæ adversus Te & Me deliquerunt.
Et nunc (Domine) quoniam mihi Cor dedisti quo ad Te precer, audi & accepta quæ coram Te vota facio.
Si Me & Regna mea in misericordia velis reminisci, perpetuando lucem Evangelii tui, & veram inter nos Religionem stabiliendo:
Reddendo Legum beneficium, & debitam Iustitiæ administrationem:
Compescendo illa plurima in Ecclesia Schismata & Factiones in statu:
Restituendo Me & meos in Iura illa antiqua & Decessorum nostrorum Gloriam:
Si Tu velis convertere corda Populi mei, ut Tibi pietate, mihi fidelitate, sibi invicem charitate uniantur:
Si hæc tandem velis Flammas extinguere, & Civilis Belli fomitem subtrahere:
Si nos publice consulendi libertate benedixe-

page.notes: No marginal notes on this page. Show-through from the reverse is visible along the left edge and was left out. The first word of the page is partly worn and uncertain (read as "mundioris"); the first word of the Satient line ("mcæ") is doubtful. The Greek running head is transcribed in Greek letters as printed. The catchword "ris," is at the foot right, and the last line ends on a hyphenated word, so the text ends on "benedixe-".
